answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-backed grove of completed work: every finished job is signed and linked into a public grove of verifiable history, and reputation accrues only from completed, dispute-free jobs over time. A quill, a single signed claim of skill, is worthless alone; it must be backed by matching jobs in the grove. Each sybil starts on an empty knoll with no history and no weight, so an attacker must pay the full cost of real work for every fake identity, while an honest agent keeps the reputation it already earned.
